title: Cloud sessions III: the queue's refs travel through a dispatched workflow
goal: A cloud session's git proxy pushes refs/heads/* only (refs/claims/*, refs/closed/* and the other queue namespaces get HTTP 403 at receive-pack) and every GitHub REST write path is refused, but a workflow_dispatch through the GitHub MCP server is accepted and an Actions job's GITHUB_TOKEN pushes any ref the rulesets leave open (scripts/auto-merge-pr.sh already writes refs/merged and refs/verified that way). Add .github/workflows/queue.yml (workflow_dispatch; inputs op=claim|renew|release|abandon|close-receipt, task, agent, branch, scopes, head, hours, reason) that checks the branch out, installs the released susi and runs the queue operation server-side, so the compare-and-swap pushes happen where they are allowed; and give susi tasks claim/renew/release/close a transport that, when the direct push is refused with a 403, dispatches that workflow (gh workflow run, or the MCP tool from Claude Code) and polls git ls-remote for the ref with a bounded wait. Pin the client side in tests/cloud_session.rs with a fake remote that refuses the push. workflow_dispatch fires only for a workflow file on the default branch, so the first landing needs one claim made outside the cloud (docs/cloud-sessions.md, GitHub from the container). As built: the transport is a push-triggered workflow rather than a dispatched one — the binary cannot call the MCP dispatch tool and a workflow_dispatch only fires for a file already on main, while a push runs the workflow file of the pushed commit. A refused push whose leases still hold becomes a commit on refs/heads/susi-queue/<agent>/<nonce> (HEAD's tree, the transaction in the message); queue.yml replays it with scripts/queue-relay.py, which writes the queue's namespaces only, and deletes the request; the client waits for that and reads the refs back. No bootstrap: a branch's first request carries the workflow itself.
